newsitem.title: USA: Port of New Orleans works to reopen shipping lanes.
newsitem.headline: Port of New Orleans works to reopen shipping lanes.

text.p: Shipping continued to be restricted along the Mississippi River after a freighter accident over the weekend but the Port of New Orleans was expected to be back to normal operations within 24 hours, port officials said on Monday.
"Working with the Coast Guard, we anticipate that we should be back to full, normal operations within 24 hours," Ron Brinson, port director, said.

The freighter MV Bright Field, a 735-foot cargo ship loaded with 64,000 tonnes of corn, collided with the New Orleans Riverwalk waterfront shopping complex on Saturday after losing steering power as it navigated downstream.
The port is a key waterway into the U.S. Midwest, and shipping along the section of the river passing New Orleans was restricted to 30-foot draft ships upriver and 20 foot-draft ships downriver.

Larger deep-draft freighters and oil tankers were still unable to make the down-bound trip because of concerns their wakes would disrupt the Bright Field, which appears to be holding up the wharf and sections of the shopping complex.
"It's important that we get river traffic back to a safe, normal operation as quickly as possible," Brinson said.

Paddle-wheelers and casino-gaming boats plying the waters of the Mississippi along the New Orleans waterfront and its historic French Quarter were cleared to return to service on Monday by the U.S. Coast Guard.
